title: Report a score with its uncertainty
statement: Report every score, sub-score or mastery estimate with its own uncertainty, such as a standard error or a floor or ceiling flag, never as a bare number.
example: Scores of 7/10 and 6/10 may differ by no more than the margin of measurement error.
detail: A Grade 3 reading red-team standard lists among its item-construction criteria that mastery and score outputs carry a certainty band, not a bare one-shot score, drawn from an assessment BrainLift. That BrainLift calls treating a score as more precise and meaningful than it is the most common inferential error with multiple-choice results, and asks for the uncertainty to be acknowledged and for decisions to rest on several data points. An interim test built as a proxy for an outside reading test applies the rule: before linking, its reports carry a 'not a RIT score' label, floor and ceiling flags and standard errors.
against: The widening factor comes from a validation run that took the provisional difficulties as the true ones (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/03_SIMULATION_EVIDENCE.md`, line 103), so it cannot reflect their error, which the package puts at σ ≈ 0.5–1.0 logits (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/02_ITEM_BANK.md`, line 264); a factor of 1.02 probably understates the real uncertainty. The package also shows domain sub-scores in every session before any factor analysis has checked the domains (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/00_CASE_FOR_APPROVAL.md`, line 146).

evidence.quote: Mastery/score outputs carry a certainty band, not a bare one-shot score
The most common inferential error in MCQ-based assessment is treating a score as more precise and more meaningful than it is.
A student who scores 7/10 and a student who scores 6/10 may not differ meaningfully in their understanding — the difference may be within the margin of measurement error.
When communicating MCQ results, acknowledge the uncertainty.
When making decisions based on MCQ results, use multiple data points
Pre-linking reports carry "not a RIT score" labels, floor/ceiling flags, and SEs.

One honesty instrument shipped with the score report itself: because provisional b values understate true score uncertainty, reports emit a **b-uncertainty-adjusted SE** — the Fisher SE inflated by the current validation run's RMSE/SEM ratio (1.02 under v4) — with an explicit `se_basis` field naming the adjustment; it is removed automatically once empirical calibration lands
